speaker: Doctor
text: I have noted your symptoms of postmenopausal bleeding and the presence of an adnexal mass. To begin our investigation, have you experienced any abdominal pain, changes in bowel habits, or symptoms of urinary frequency or urgency?

speaker: Patient
text: 65-year-old woman. The patient presents with a 2-month history of intermittent postmenopausal bleeding. She denies any recent weight loss, fever, or changes in bladder or bowel habits. No previous history of similar symptoms. She has no history of serious illness and takes no medications regularly.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for that information. Since you have no pain or urinary changes, could you describe the size of the adnexal mass noted on your exam and whether you have noticed any vaginal discharge? Also, have you had a Pap smear or pelvic ultrasound in the last year?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Intermittent bleeding from the vagina. I also have No recent weight loss, No fever, No changes in bladder or bowel habits.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Endometrial Hyperplasia with or without Atypia (considering Atypical Hyperplasia or Early Endometrial Carcinoma given postmenopausal bleeding and lack of pain).

REQUEST TEST: Transvaginal Ultrasound (TVUS) to measure endometrial thickness.
REQUEST TEST: Endometrial Biopsy.
